title: A reply still being stored no longer costs its session the newest turn at eviction
question: Council CR-20260924-ninfer-durable-evict-r1 (daybreak-blue R2) found that save-before-evict gave a victim's reply two seconds to reach the response store and then let the engine drop its continuation. A streamed reply is stored only after its last delta reaches the client, so a slow reader loses exactly the newest turn the handler protects. Does it happen on the shipped RTX 5090 profile, and does the remediation close it?
answer: Yes, and yes. With the reply held out of the store for 6 s while another ceiling-class session's admission had to evict it, the reviewed candidate c5fe23db gave up after 2 s, evicted the session, refused its automatic save and its graceful-stop save (`saved 0, nothing to save 1, refused 1`, `their state is lost`), and after a restart the held turn answered 404 previous_response_not_found. The remediated a4d26ccb deferred, saved the session as soon as the reply was stored, then evicted it; the stop reported `saved 0, nothing to save 2, refused 0` and after a restart the held turn answered the code it introduced exactly.

fixes.source: alphastorm/ninfer branch fix/durable-session-eviction, remediation of council CR-20260924-ninfer-durable-evict-r1 on c5fe23db

commits.30cfdf83: fix(serve): stop evicting other sessions once a quota reclamation fails - a pass whose reclamation failed no longer evicts other sessions' current checkpoints; the save is refused or usage stays over the cap by the stuck bytes (daybreak-blue R1, claude R1)
commits.5c18af62: fix(serve): settle automatic retry budgets on every final outcome - the retry table holds a session only while its retry is queued (daybreak-blue R3)
commits.a4d26ccb: fix(runtime): keep a pressure victim resident while its reply is being stored - stored Responses turns hold a ResponsePublication until stored or abandoned; the handler reports Settled or Pending per victim and the engine drops only settled ones; transient save refusals are Pending up to six times (daybreak-blue R2, claude R2)

method.tracer: A throwaway tracer, retained with the review evidence (sha256 below): a one-shot gdb breakpoint on ninfer::serve::ResponseStore::put in non-stop mode, from a sidecar container sharing the arm's PID namespace, holds the first thread to reach it for 6 s while every other thread runs, then lets it continue and detaches. It is the reviewer's verification step: barrier the store publication for more than two seconds after the engine catalogues the turn.
method.workload: Shipped RTX 5090 profile (qwen38-5090-v0.7.0 arguments, --binary-sha256 set per arm). EXP-050's prefix: a 130,048-token long-context conversation, then session V's 126,128-token base turn and its automatic checkpoint. With the barrier armed, V's short second turn introduces the code V-9241 and is held at put; as soon as the barrier fires, session W's 126,128-token base turn arrives, whose admission must evict V (as EXP-050's second 126K base evicted the first). Thinking off, greedy. A graceful stop follows, then a restart on the same checkpoint root and one continuation of V from its held turn asking for that code.
method.arms: c5fe23db is the frozen subject the council reviewed; a4d26ccb is its remediation. One run each, production stopped under the lane supervisor hold and restored afterwards.

host_tests: a4d26ccb: Linux sm_120a appliance build 8/8 suites; RTX 4090 native MSVC build 9/9. The failed-reclamation store regression fails 4 checks against c5fe23db's store and passes at a4d26ccb.
conclusion: Save-before-evict now waits on the reply's actual publication instead of a fixed guess, so a turn that is still reaching its client is saved before its session is evicted. The waiting request pays for it: W was admitted once the save finished, 15.8 s after the hold began, instead of 2.2 s; its queue deadline bounds that wait.
limits: One run per arm, RTX 5090 only; the RTX 4090 native build passes the same host suites and qualification must still force a checkpoint-tagged eviction there.
The hold is a debugger barrier, not a slow network client; it isolates the store's lag behind the engine, which a slow reader produces through blocked delta writes.
A request waiting behind a pending victim can time out if the reply takes longer than its queue deadline to be stored; it is not retried by the server.
The transient-refusal branch of the same outcome contract was not exercised at runtime.
